newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Yilmaz in coalition talks with leftist.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Yilmaz in coalition talks with leftist.

text.p: Turkish secularist Mesut Yilmaz was to hold talks with a leftist leader on Thursday on forming an anti-Islamist coalition, his office said.
A spokesman said prime minister-designate Yilmaz would meet Democratic Left Party leader Bulent Ecevit at 1100 GMT in the parliament building.
Ecevit, an avowed secularist, has said he is prepared to join a planned left-right government to keep the Islamists of Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan out of office.
The Turkish press says former prime minister Ecevit could be in line for a cabinet post in the planned coalition.

Main opposition leader Yilmaz is just short of the simple majority needed to win a vote of confidence in the 550-member parliament and so needs further defections from the Islamists' True Path Party conservative allies.
Yilmaz said on Wednesday night he was not worried by a petition signed by 278 MPs who vowed not to vote for him in any confidence vote.
"Our government will comfortably win a confidence vote," the Anatolian news agency quoted him as saying.
Some anti-Islamist MPs from Tansu Ciller's True Path who signed the petition say nevertheless that they will not turn up at a confidence vote, thus helping Yilmaz.
